Nottawaseppi Huron Band of Potawatomi Indians

The Nottawaseppi Huron Band of the Potawatomi has a distinct community history centered on Pine Creek in Michigan. The Band’s public account describes return after removal and a prolonged recognition effort, concluding with federal recognition in1995. It offers a direct community voice and a starting chronology. A separately identified enterprise image shows one institution associated with the Band; it should not stand for all of the community’s culture, history or present life.

Return and persistence

Read the Band’s account of people returning to Michigan after removal alongside its discussion of federal recognition efforts. A policy or removal narrative does not mean that every family experienced the same journey.

02

The scope of the photograph

FireKeepers is a named Band enterprise, and the official account dates its opening to2009. The photograph is an exterior view from that year, not a portrait of Tribal members or evidence of present economic conditions.

History ↗

The Band connects Pine Creek community continuity with resistance to removal and its1995 recognition. The page is a concise community narrative rather than a complete treaty or family history.

Scope: Entire displayed four-paragraph History body read. Original treaty texts, acknowledgment files, membership histories and present legal entitlements were not inspected in this bounded review.
